question: An AI governance owner / AI CoE exists with executive sponsorship.
AI use cases are inventoried and risk-classified before build.
Responsible AI principles are documented and applied as review gates.
Every AI agent has a first-class identity (Entra Agent ID), not a shared app/service principal.
Every agent has a named human sponsor accountable for its lifecycle.
Conditional Access and least-privilege access packages apply to agents.
Sensitivity labels and DLP govern what data AI/agents can access and return.
DSPM for AI surfaces oversharing/exfiltration risk for AI apps and agents.
AI interactions are captured in audit logs and discoverable (eDiscovery).
AI workloads are discovered and posture-assessed (Defender AI-SPM / AI-BOM).
Runtime threat protection and Prompt Shields defend against injection/jailbreak.
AI security alerts are correlated in the SOC (Defender XDR).
Agents/models are evaluated for quality and safety before deployment.
Evaluation runs as a CI/CD gate on changes.
Continuous evaluation monitors production for drift/regression.
AI systems are red-teamed (automated and/or manual) before release.
Attack Success Rate is tracked over time as a break-fix metric.
Indirect prompt injection (XPIA) is specifically tested for agents.
A registry provides a single source of truth for all agents (incl. shadow agents).
Agent lifecycle (onboard→monitor→decommission) is centrally managed.
Governance posture is measured and reported to leadership.
